claims.claim: Sweet Home upheld the earlier habitat-related harm definition; the 2026 rescission is an agency action, not a Supreme Court reversal of that decision.
claims.limitations: Does not resolve later challenges to the rescission.

claims.claim: The 2024 rules revised portions of the 2019 listing and consultation framework and restored the FWS blanket protection option. They did not repeal every 2019 provision.
claims.limitations: Framework changes do not themselves establish improved welfare.

claims.claim: The April 2025 harm proposal became a July 14, 2026 final rule, effective September 14. It removes regulatory definitions, while harm remains in the statutory definition of take.
claims.locator: 91 FR43300 Dates and Background; final amendments
claims.limitations: Judicial interpretation and enforcement remain material; no claim that all habitat destruction became lawful.

claims.claim: Effective August 20, 2026, FWS removed the future blanket-rule option, preserving existing threatened-species protections. Species-specific rules remain available; removal does not mean every newly threatened species lacks protection.
claims.limitations: FWS rule, not a change to NMFS's separate threatened-species program.

claims.claim: The 2026 critical-habitat exclusion procedure is final; separate listing and consultation revisions are still described as proposals on the current FWS status page.
claims.locator: 91 FR45662 Dates; status page Final Rules / Proposed Rules
claims.evidenceType: Final rule and agency status page
claims.limitations: Status-page freshness and later court orders require continued checking.

claims.claim: Obama's January 2017 opinion endorsed incidental-take coverage. Trump I reversed the interpretation, and the Southern District of New York vacated that opinion in August 2020.
claims.locator: Court opinion background and conclusion; 86 FR1134
claims.limitations: Circuit interpretations differ; this is not a Supreme Court holding.

claims.claim: Trump I's January 2021 regulation excluded incidental take. Biden revoked it effective December 3, 2021, returning to incidental-take coverage subject to judicial precedent and enforcement discretion.
claims.limitations: No standardized mortality counterfactual is established by these rules.

claims.claim: M-37085 reinstates the 2017 exclusion interpretation as binding within DOI, except actions relying on it within the Southern District of New York's jurisdiction.
claims.limitations: Agency interpretation does not amend the statute or settle conflicting judicial interpretations.

claims.claim: Trump II withdrew the 2021 advance notice for incidental-take authorization; FWS's May 2026 presentation also reports rescission of Director's Order 225.
claims.evidenceType: Withdrawal notice and agency implementation report
claims.limitations: The advance notice was a rulemaking initiative, not an operational general permit program.

claims.claim: FBI began collecting a distinct animal-cruelty category in NIBRS on January 1, 2016.
claims.limitations: Captures reporting to participating police agencies, not all cruelty.

claims.claim: Population coverage of agencies reporting at least one month grew from 33.9% in 2017 to 87.3% in 2024; these are general NIBRS coverage figures.
claims.limitations: Not a stable cohort or a denominator of animals; cannot establish cruelty trends.

claims.claim: NIBRS cruelty records do not describe individual animal victims, and some participating agencies may not report animal cruelty.
claims.limitations: Study assesses 2020 data; does not estimate current missingness.

claims.claim: PETS required planning for household pets and service animals and authorized related emergency assistance.
claims.limitations: No comparable survival or reunification series assembled.

claims.claim: A study published in 2000 reported that 20 of 22 audited slaughter plants rendered all observed cattle insensible before hoisting.
claims.limitations: Plant pass count, not share of all US cattle; private audit sample, no causal presidential attribution.

claims.claim: The 1999 law added a commercial-depiction offense with a five-year maximum and a serious-value exception.
claims.limitations: Does not establish reduced cruelty.

claims.claim: On April 20, 2010, the Supreme Court held the 1999 §48 substantially overbroad under the First Amendment, affirming vacatur of Stevens's conviction.
claims.limitations: Invalidation concerned the depiction statute, not permission to commit underlying cruelty.

claims.claim: P.L.110-22 established felony penalties up to three years and prohibited interstate/foreign trade in bird-fighting sharp implements.
claims.limitations: The original penalty is historical and was replaced in 2008.

claims.claim: Current federal animal-fighting statutes retain the equipment prohibition; ordinary covered violations carry up to five years, attendance up to one, and causing under-16 attendance up to three.
claims.limitations: Code verified through October 9, 2026; maximums do not describe actual sentences.

claims.claim: The 2008 amendment added possession/training offenses, expanded the commerce formulation, and increased the maximum to five years; the corrected enactment operates from May 22, 2008.
claims.limitations: Does not isolate incremental deterrent effect.

claims.claim: Congress enacted P.L.110-246 over George W. Bush's veto on June 18, 2008; describing this as a presidential signing is incorrect.
claims.limitations: An omnibus veto does not establish the president's position on this individual provision.

claims.claim: Amendment 800 raised the ordinary animal-fighting base offense level from 10 to 16, effective November 1, 2016. Its pooled FY2011–2014 sample contained 74 offenders at base level 10; 31.0% received above-range sentences.
claims.locator: Higher Penalties for Animal Fighting Venture Offenses; Effective Date
claims.limitations: Selected sentenced-offender population; no untreated comparator for animal-welfare effects; not an annual series.

claims.claim: The 2010 rewrite limited covered animal-crush videos to obscene depictions, with commerce-related creation/distribution offenses, exceptions, and a seven-year maximum.
claims.limitations: Legislative findings about incentives are not causal evaluation.

claims.claim: In 2017 the Fifth Circuit acquitted Brent Justice on one video-creation count for lack of the required obscenity element and affirmed the other three convictions.
claims.limitations: Unpublished decision; one count's reversal did not require resentencing because concurrent terms were identical.

claims.claim: The 2014 farm bill made knowing attendance at a covered animal fight punishable by up to one year and causing a child under 16 to attend punishable by up to three years.
claims.limitations: The child threshold is under 16.

claims.claim: DOJ reported Anderson's October 6, 2021 sentences of 18 months each for conspiracy and causing under-16 attendance, served concurrently.
claims.limitations: Both records are DOJ publications; judgment and subsequent supervision outcomes not independently obtained.

claims.claim: The 2018 law removed remaining live-bird local-law exceptions effective December 20, 2019, including exceptions important in U.S. territories.
claims.limitations: Existing prohibitions on attendance and other activities predated this extension.

claims.claim: The First Circuit upheld challenged application of the territorial extension to Puerto Rico on January 14, 2021.
claims.limitations: A constitutional decision is not evidence of compliance or reduced suffering.

claims.claim: PACT added §48(a)(1), a purposeful animal-crushing conduct offense with a federal jurisdictional connection; video offenses remain separately defined.
claims.limitations: Only video offenses require obscenity; do not transfer that requirement to the conduct offense.

claims.claim: PACT covers the enumerated mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians, with substantial activity exceptions; it does not criminalize all animal cruelty or all harmful agriculture/research practices.
claims.limitations: Exceptions and jurisdictional elements require case-specific interpretation. Fish/invertebrates are not enumerated.

claims.claim: DOJ reported Krystal Scott's conviction under §48(a), 30 months' imprisonment, and five years' supervised release in November 2021.
claims.limitations: Primary sentencing judgment and precise subsection/animal count not retrieved.

claims.claim: DOJ reported Kenneth Herrera's December 20, 2023 sentence of 12 months and one day, three years of supervision, and $5,000 fine for video-related offenses.
claims.limitations: A post-PACT video case is not proof that the newly added conduct offense was necessary.

claims.claim: DOJ reported in October 2026 that Desmond Brown received 60 months' imprisonment and three years' supervision for animal crushing; the supervision conditions bar animal possession.
claims.limitations: Release date is October 15, 2026; exact judgment date and appeal status were not separately verified.

claims.claim: DOJ reported Gray's 2025 guilty plea and 15-month sentence for a dogfighting venture and unlawful firearm possession; 14 dogs were seized.
claims.limitations: Mixed offenses; seizure is an intervention count, not final rehabilitation/adoption outcomes or a causal estimate.

claims.claim: APHIS reported 17 initiated AWA investigative cases in FY2019, 262 in each of FY2022 and FY2023, and 240 in FY2025. These are administrative outputs, not counts of abused animals or estimates of deterrence.
claims.locator: Animal Welfare / Animal Care enforcement sections
claims.limitations: Cases initiated, warnings, orders and inspections differ in grain and time lag. FY2021 and FY2025 straddle administrations. No animal-exposure denominator. The CRS 2022 summary differs from the fiscal budget totals and remains unreconciled.

claims.claim: OIG found unreliable ACIS queries and inadequately addressed or documented responses for 145 of 322 dog-breeder complaints reviewed from FY2017–FY2019. APHIS replaced ACIS in September 2020 and agreed to control improvements.
claims.limitations: The audit could not evaluate actual breeder compliance because COVID-19 limited fieldwork; documentation failure is not proof that every complaint was ignored.

claims.claim: Reported AWA inspections fell from 9,326 in FY2019 to 5,620 in pandemic FY2020, then reached 10,595 in FY2022. Licensed/registered entity counts changed substantially; inspections may revisit an entity.
claims.limitations: Counts are activity, not the fraction of unique facilities inspected; eFile transition and virtual inspections complicate comparability.

claims.claim: The budget notes also give a consistent five-year series for inspections of USDA Agricultural Research Service facilities: 47, 48, 49, 59 and 56 for FY2019–FY2023, against 38, 38, 38, 39 and 43 registered facilities.
claims.locator: Animal Welfare; Agricultural Research Service facilities
claims.limitations: A narrow federal research subset, not all AWA facilities; repeated inspections mean visits per facility, not inspection coverage.

claims.claim: USDA removed public database access in February 2017. Congress subsequently required a searchable AWA database in P.L.116-94 (7 USC 2146a), and APHIS launched it in September 2020.
claims.limitations: The access change is verified; its net effect on animal abuse was not measured.

claims.claim: APHIS currently advertises searchable licensee/registrant records, inspection reports, research annual reports and enforcement records.
claims.locator: USDA Animal Care Public Search Tool; modified 2025-11-17
claims.limitations: Availability is not proof of completeness or consistent historical redaction.

claims.claim: The Obama-era 2013 rule narrowed the retail-pet-store exemption to transactions with buyer, seller and animal physically present, bringing otherwise covered sight-unseen sellers under licensing and inspection. It also expanded the small-breeder exemption from three to four breeding females.
claims.limitations: Not every internet seller is covered; qualifying small breeders and in-person sellers remain exempt. Forecasted coverage is not actual enforcement.

claims.claim: Trump I's 2020 rule replaced annual license renewal with a compliance demonstration for a new three-year license and strengthened dog-care standards, including continuously available potable water and veterinary-care requirements.
claims.limitations: Licensing applies to regulated dealers and exhibitors, not all dog owners; minimum standards do not quantify welfare effects.

claims.claim: APHIS reported 1,485 relicense inspections in FY2023 and completion of the three-year transition in September 2023. Its 2026 guidance still specifies continuous potable water for regulated dogs.
claims.locator: FY2025 explanatory notes Animal Welfare; 9 CFR 3.10 guidance
claims.limitations: Inspection activity confirms implementation under Biden, not that all dogs received improved care.

claims.claim: In each FY2017–FY2022, DQPs recorded more performance-horse noncompliances per inspected entry at events with APHIS present than without it. FY2022 ratios were 219/3,220 and 174/9,746; these do not establish fractions of unique noncompliant horses.
claims.limitations: APHIS event selection and entry selection are not random; the groups may overlap. Includes violations beyond soring and is not a causal estimate of monitoring.

claims.claim: APHIS reported 78 recorded sore noncompliances per 1,556 inspected entries in FY2018 and 525 per 2,740 in FY2023. These detection ratios cannot establish population prevalence or the number of unique sore horses.
claims.limitations: Selected entries, not unique horses; two-veterinarian confirmation requirement was removed in 2021. This series includes referrals omitted from event-activity summaries.

claims.claim: After the 2017 rule was withdrawn before publication, the D.C. Circuit held in 2022 that withdrawal after public inspection required notice and comment. Biden's USDA formally withdrew it in 2023 while developing a replacement.
claims.limitations: Procedural ruling did not measure outcomes or itself implement the 2017 protections.

claims.claim: Biden's May 2024 rule sought to replace industry DQPs with APHIS-authorized inspectors. Section 11.19 training authorization took effect June 7, 2024. Following partial January 2025 vacatur, Trump II postponed the main surviving amendments to December 31, 2026; APHIS's October 2026 page reports training paused.
claims.locator: 89 FR 39194; 91 FR 3633–3635; HPA Final Rule Postponement
claims.limitations: The main delayed amendments take effect after the cutoff; §11.19 is already effective. Do not describe the entire rule as either implemented or not effective, or infer prevented soring.

claims.claim: Obama's January 2017 OLPP standards were withdrawn by Trump I in March 2018. Biden's November 2023 OLPS rule reinstated and revised federal organic livestock/poultry husbandry standards.
claims.limitations: Applies through voluntary USDA organic certification, not a universal farm-welfare law.

claims.claim: OLPS became effective January 12, 2024. Most compliance was due January 2, 2025; specified requirements for existing poultry operations run to January 2, 2029. A September 2026 AMS collection notice still describes OLPS administration.
claims.limitations: Legal deadlines and ongoing administration do not establish actual compliance or animal outcomes; transition remains incomplete.

claims.claim: The 2009 final rule requires condemnation of cattle that become non-ambulatory after ante-mortem inspection, closing an exception left by the 2004 rule. USDA proposed the change in 2008 and finalized it under Obama.
claims.limitations: Official slaughter establishments; not a farm-wide ban, not a rule for every livestock species. Food-safety and welfare purposes overlap.

claims.claim: FSIS's current ante-mortem directive maintains the non-ambulatory-cattle rule but notes a distinct custom-slaughter situation for cattle becoming disabled after delivery and otherwise eligible for human food.
claims.locator: Directive 6100.1 Revision 3; Background and custom slaughter
claims.limitations: Custom exemption must not be mistaken for a general exception at inspected commercial slaughter plants.

claims.claim: Obama's 2016 rule removed the option of holding non-ambulatory veal calves for rest and warming to see whether they recovered. It requires prompt humane euthanasia; implementation began September 16, 2016.
claims.limitations: Eliminates a handling incentive, but the reviewed sources do not supply a national pre/post causal evaluation.

claims.claim: GAO reported humane-handling enforcement resources of 110, 124, 121, 157 and 157 FTEs in FY2005–FY2009. Congressional minimums were 63, 63, no requirement, 83 and 120.
claims.limitations: FTEs are allocated time, not a dedicated staff headcount or a controlled explanation of welfare changes.

claims.claim: GAO found inconsistent enforcement and knowledge gaps concerning signs of sensibility, alongside higher recorded resources. The audit recommended stronger guidance, training and oversight; FSIS disputed some findings.
claims.limitations: Historical audit; does not establish current conditions or that additional staff caused better outcomes.

claims.claim: A peer-reviewed review found 293 posted humane-handling enforcement actions in 2018–2020; 251 concerned stunning and 233 involved suspending or reinstating suspension of inspection pending corrective action.
claims.limitations: Letters measure detected events and regulatory responses, not unique animals or all violations; repeat actions can concern the same establishment.

claims.claim: Trump I's 2019 NSIS rule allowed voluntary swine-inspection changes and removed the 1,106-head-per-hour maximum. A 2021 court decision vacated the line-speed provision for inadequate consideration of worker-safety comments; it did not find animal-welfare effects.
claims.limitations: Other NSIS provisions continued; worker-safety findings must not be relabeled animal-welfare results.

claims.claim: The 2026 proposal reports that six Time-Limited Trial plants had 11 humane-handling noncompliance records across 25,821 verification tasks from each waiver's start through February 28, 2025, with none classified egregious.
claims.limitations: Selected participants, pooled periods, task-level denominator, agency classification and no control group. This is not the percentage of pigs treated inhumanely.

claims.claim: Trump II proposed restoring unlimited NSIS line speeds, conditional on process control, on February 19, 2026. The latest verified August 5 agency update says comments were under review.
claims.locator: 91 FR 7905; Latest Regulatory and Program Updates
claims.limitations: No final rule was identified in this research; the August update alone cannot exclude a later action before the cutoff.

claims.claim: Published HPA event reports list 2,740 USDA-inspected entries in FY2023 and 2,031 in FY2024. The FY2025 report snapshot, dated September 23 before fiscal year-end, lists 314 inspected entries and 100 horses radiographed.
claims.limitations: Selected event lists and changing inspection/radiography mix; FY2025 snapshot is not confirmed complete. Counts show reported activity, not incidence or causal effects of the rule delay.

claims.claim: The law restricts possession and breeding and bars direct public contact; conditional exceptions remain.
claims.limitations: The cited source does not estimate a causal animal-welfare effect.

claims.claim: FWS reports June 12, 2023 implementation and a June 18 registration deadline; these are implementation milestones, not measured reductions in suffering.
claims.limitations: The cited source does not estimate a causal animal-welfare effect.

claims.claim: The fin-sales law took effect December 23, 2022; it does not prohibit all shark fishing or trade in whole sharks.
claims.limitations: The cited source does not estimate a causal animal-welfare effect.

claims.claim: NOAA reports zero declared shark-fin exports in 2023 and cessation of reported imports before the December 2022 sales ban. NOAA records conflict on the 2019 import value, which is withheld pending reconciliation; trade figures do not establish that shark mortality ended.
claims.locator: 2024 Shark Finning Report PDF p. 8; 2020 HMS SAFE Table 8.30, printed p. 211 (PDF p. 234), 2019 row
claims.limitations: Customs declarations omit undetected illegal trade; no untreated comparison. The 2020 SAFE table reports preliminary 2019 imports of 1 metric ton, while the 2024 narrative can be read as zero from or after 2019; revisions or wording may explain the difference, but this review has not reconciled it.

claims.claim: 21 USC 355 expressly permits several nonclinical methods and continues to list animal tests.
claims.limitations: The cited source does not estimate a causal animal-welfare effect.

claims.claim: FDA's antibody guidance remained labeled draft and not for implementation on the retrieved page; the April 2026 milestone announcement is not independent proof of realized animal savings.
claims.limitations: The cited sources do not supply sponsor-level uptake or counterfactual animal counts.

claims.claim: The 2025 NIH policy broadens funding opportunities; it does not prohibit grants using only animal models when scientifically justified.
claims.limitations: The cited source does not estimate a causal animal-welfare effect.

claims.claim: Complement-ARIE concept approval occurred in January 2024; first awards and ORIVA were announced in March and June 2026 respectively.
claims.limitations: The cited source does not estimate a causal animal-welfare effect.

claims.claim: NIH ended support for invasive chimpanzee research while continuing eligible noninvasive work; the 2025 process update retains the 2016 policy.
claims.limitations: The cited source does not estimate a causal animal-welfare effect.

claims.claim: GAO found 561 NIH-owned/supported chimpanzees on January 15, 2016, including 179 at Chimp Haven; eligibility did not mean all had moved.
claims.limitations: 2016 census only.

claims.claim: A 2023 paper found increased habitat use over time in 18 chimpanzees observed in 2005; it is supporting husbandry evidence, not an evaluation of the 2015 policy.
claims.limitations: Single site, small sample, habitat and social changes combined; no policy control group.

claims.claim: AWA research totals cannot be presented as all U.S. laboratory animals; statutory exclusions and reporting population limit the denominator.
claims.limitations: The cited source does not estimate a causal animal-welfare effect.

claims.claim: NIH said October 1, 2026 that annual OLAW reports do not require animal numbers; its broader annual-reporting change remained a proposal.
claims.limitations: The cited source does not estimate a causal animal-welfare effect.

claims.claim: APHIS FY2021–2025 reports distinguish held/not used (B) from used categories C, D and E. Neither category E nor declining animal counts measures aggregate suffering.
claims.limitations: Data may be amended; new avian regulation and reporting categories affect total-series comparability; no causal design.

claims.claim: APHIS phased bird-standard compliance between August 2023 and February 2024; this did not remove the AWA's purpose-bred research-bird exclusion.
claims.limitations: The cited source does not estimate a causal animal-welfare effect.

claims.claim: The 2024 final rule restored the baiting restriction but did not enact every hunting restriction in its proposal.
claims.limitations: The cited source does not estimate a causal animal-welfare effect.

claims.claim: DOI's October 16, 2026 announcement set publication for October 19 and effectiveness 30 days later; treating the replacement as already effective at the cutoff would be incorrect.
claims.limitations: Could not retrieve final Federal Register document 2026-21299; cannot assert exact final regulatory text.

claims.claim: Federal ivory restrictions effective July 6, 2016 allow conditional exceptions and do not generally ban lawful personal possession.
claims.locator: Effective-date, possession and interstate-commerce FAQ sections
claims.limitations: The cited source does not estimate a causal animal-welfare effect.

claims.claim: The 2024 elephant amendment addresses live imports/captive care and separate permitting; conservation purpose is not proof of reduced individual suffering.
claims.locator: Live African elephant imports and domestic benefit questions
claims.limitations: No outcome study isolating the rule was located in this review.

claims.claim: FDA published a direct final terminology rule and companion proposed rule September 22, 2026; the direct final rule was not effective by October 19 and could be withdrawn following significant adverse comments.
claims.limitations: Scheduled February 4, 2027 effective date is outside cutoff; no assumption of future effectiveness.

cases.caseName: Natural Resources Defense Council, Inc. v. U.S. Department of the Interior
cases.court: U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York
cases.penalty: Not applicable: administrative judicial review, not a criminal animal count.
cases.followup: Appeal dismissed March 2, 2021 at government's request; 2025 DOI memorandum preserves an SDNY exception.
cases.limitations: Selected precedent; no prosecution, animal total, or national case census.

cases.caseName: United States v. Robert J. Stevens
cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States; underlying W.D. Pennsylvania
cases.disposition: Three trial convictions were vacated by the Third Circuit; Supreme Court affirmed invalidation.
cases.penalty: Original concurrent 37-month sentences and three years' supervised release were attached to the vacated convictions.
cases.followup: 2010 replacement statute enacted; this case is a failed conviction, not a successful enforcement outcome.
cases.limitations: Animal suffering prevented cannot be inferred; sale-of-depictions prosecution, not a conviction for the underlying fights.

cases.court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit; underlying S.D. Texas
cases.disposition: Three video-related convictions affirmed; one video-creation conviction vacated with judgment of acquittal.
cases.penalty: 57-month concurrent terms; opinion reports 14 months after credit for related state custody.
cases.followup: No resentencing required after reversal of one count; opinion is unpublished.
cases.limitations: Do not report all four original convictions as upheld, combine federal/state penalties, or treat sentence as an animal-welfare outcome.

cases.caseName: United States v. Odell S. Anderson, Sr.
cases.court: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia
cases.disposition: Guilty plea to dogfighting conspiracy and causing a child under 16 to attend.
cases.penalty: 18 months on each count, concurrently; three years' supervised release.
cases.followup: Agency reports sentence; completion, recidivism, and animal placement not established.
cases.limitations: Bulletin gives Nos.3:21-CR-00023–00026 for multi-defendant group without mapping a specific docket to Anderson; left null. Do not add the concurrent terms.

cases.caseName: United States v. Krystal Cherika Scott
cases.court: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana
cases.disposition: Found guilty; sentenced for animal crushing.
cases.penalty: DOJ reports 30 months' imprisonment and five years' supervised release.
cases.followup: Release was updated February 26, 2024; no independently retrieved post-sentence record.
cases.limitations: Date denotes sentencing-report publication. Judgment not obtained, including verification of reported supervised-release term. Exact number of animals not supplied.

cases.caseName: United States v. Kenneth J. Herrera
cases.court: U.S. District Court for the Western District of Wisconsin
cases.statute: 18 U.S.C. §48 video provisions; release describes PACT Act
cases.disposition: Guilty plea for creating, selling and distributing an animal-crushing video, as described by DOJ.
cases.penalty: 12 months and one day imprisonment; three years' supervised release; $5,000 fine.
cases.followup: No completed supervision or recidivism outcome retrieved.
cases.limitations: One monkey is described in the charged video, not a total case-victim census. A video case cannot establish incremental effect of PACT's new conduct offense.

cases.caseName: United States v. Samuel Alexander Gray
cases.court: U.S. District Court for the District of South Carolina
cases.statute: Animal-fighting venture and felon-in-possession offenses; release omits exact statutory subsections
cases.penalty: 15 months imprisonment; three years' supervision with no dog ownership.
cases.followup: Dogs were seized following September 2023 investigation; final animal disposition not reported.
cases.limitations: Date denotes sentencing-report publication. Mixed firearm/fighting sentence cannot be attributed solely to animal-fighting law. Fourteen denotes seized dogs, not all harmed animals.

cases.caseName: United States v. Desmond Levon Brown
cases.court: U.S. District Court for the District of South Carolina
cases.statute: 18 U.S.C. §48 animal-crushing offense; release labels prosecution under PACT
cases.disposition: Sentence reported for purposeful killing of a puppy by burning.
cases.penalty: 60 months imprisonment; three years' supervision prohibiting animal ownership or possession.
cases.followup: Latest reviewed report October 15, 2026; appeal and sentence completion unknown.
cases.limitations: Date is release date, not independently verified judgment date. Agency's 'first PACT case' claim applies to South Carolina district, not the nation.

cases.caseName: Humane Society of the United States v. United States Department of Agriculture
cases.court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit
cases.statute: Administrative Procedure Act; Horse Protection Act rulemaking
cases.disposition: Reversed and remanded; withdrawal of a rule made available for public inspection required notice and comment.
cases.penalty: No criminal sentence or animal-count finding; regulatory judicial review.
cases.followup: USDA conducted notice-and-comment withdrawal in 2023 and finalized a replacement rule in 2024.
cases.limitations: Procedural decision, not a conviction or measured reduction in soring.

cases.caseName: Tennessee Walking Horse National Celebration Association et al. v. United States Department of Agriculture et al.
cases.court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas
cases.statute: Horse Protection Act; Administrative Procedure Act
cases.disposition: Partly vacated the 2024 rule, including specified equipment/substance prohibitions, dermatologic criteria and review provisions; inspector-system replacement survived.
cases.followup: USDA's January 2026 rule postponed the main non-vacated amendments until December 31, 2026; §11.19 training authorization was already effective June 7, 2024.
cases.limitations: Disposition verified through USDA's subsequent Federal Register account; district-court opinion was not independently retrieved. Do not count as animal-cruelty enforcement.

cases.caseName: Humane Society of the United States et al. v. National Institutes of Health et al.
cases.court: U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland
cases.disposition: Vacated NIH's Alamogordo transfer-ineligibility decision and remanded; required compliance with statutory sanctuary acceptance.
cases.followup: Chimp Haven reports receiving all remaining Alamogordo chimpanzees in 2025; individual transfer records not audited here.
cases.limitations: Civil judicial review, not animal-cruelty prosecution. No assumption that court alone caused later transfers.

gaps.topic: Conservation is not a welfare outcome
gaps.detail: No policy-specific causal mortality, injury or suffering estimate is supported by this legal chronology.
gaps.neededData: Species and site exposure, hazards, enforcement, prevention behavior and measured outcomes with a credible counterfactual.
gaps.impact: No lives-saved total, welfare effect size or presidential ranking.

gaps.detail: ESA status was checked against the agency's current rule page; MBTA implementation is directly corroborated through May 2026. A full court-docket audit through October 19 was not completed.
gaps.neededData: Current dockets and any later injunctions, stays, appeals, rules or memoranda.
gaps.impact: Published effective dates are reported with a status-completeness caveat.

gaps.detail: Secondary reports describe September 2026 take guidance; its primary text was not retrieved in this bounded review and its specific instructions are excluded.
gaps.neededData: Signed FWS and NMFS guidance, implementation records and judicial review.
gaps.impact: Do not infer from the regulatory rescission that every accidental killing or habitat impact is exempt.

gaps.detail: Direct older DOI links for M-37041 and M-37050 returned 404. Their history is documented using the retrieved court opinion and later primary agency records.
gaps.neededData: Archived signed opinions for a complete documentary archive.
gaps.impact: January 2017 is retained at month precision, consistent with the retrieved court record.

gaps.detail: No harmonized animal-outcome panel with defensible treatment and comparison groups was assembled.
gaps.neededData: Facility/animal-level longitudinal outcomes, stable reporting and exposure timing; appropriate comparisons.
gaps.impact: No national suffering reduction or overall presidential ranking is estimated.

gaps.detail: Historical staffing observations are partial. Comparable welfare-specific budgets and inflation series are not yet assembled.
gaps.neededData: Actual obligations and welfare-specific FTE by fiscal year; CPI or agency-appropriate deflator and consistent activity boundaries.
gaps.impact: No nominal-dollar or inflation-adjusted administration ranking.

gaps.detail: General coverage increases are documented; a constant cruelty-reporting agency panel is not validated.
gaps.neededData: Agency-month participation and offense-level completeness; local coding transitions and covered populations.
gaps.impact: Raw national cruelty counts are excluded from trend claims.

gaps.detail: The Grandin audit survey contains direct stunning/handling measures but no federal-policy comparison group.
gaps.neededData: Comparable plant outcomes before/after federal implementation, private audit histories, exposure and matched controls.
gaps.impact: Observed private audit outcomes cannot be assigned to Clinton or later presidents.

gaps.detail: Targeted searches for evaluations of the 1999 depiction law, 2007/2008 fighting laws, 2010 video law, 2014 attendance provision, 2018 territorial expansion, and the animal PACT Act did not identify a credible national causal estimate. This is a search result, not proof no study exists.
gaps.neededData: Repeatable measures of harm/prevalence, enforcement intensity, controls/counterfactual design, displacement and reporting changes.
gaps.impact: Do not claim the laws reduced cruelty by a measured amount, or infer ineffectiveness from missing evaluations.

gaps.detail: Selected DOJ releases and court opinions are not a census. Cases, defendants, charges, seizures, and sentences are different units; multi-statute prosecutions complicate attribution.
gaps.neededData: Deduplicated docket-linked national data by statute/subsection, filing and disposition dates, dismissals, convictions, and outcomes.
gaps.impact: No annual prosecution/conviction chart or presidential ranking can be built from these selected records.

gaps.detail: Research cutoff is October 19, 2026. Official Code text retrieved for §§48,49 and 7 USC2156 states currency through October 9, 2026. Latest selected agency report is October 15, 2026; this is not complete-year coverage.
gaps.neededData: Refresh Code and any intervening session laws and court decisions after October 9; obtain full-year 2026 data when published.
gaps.impact: Describe status as verified through source currency; avoid claiming complete 2026 legal or enforcement coverage.

gaps.detail: Gray release reports 14 dogs seized but no verified rehabilitation, adoption, euthanasia, or long-term welfare follow-up. Other selected records have incomplete victim counts.
gaps.neededData: Court forfeiture orders, shelter intake/disposition and veterinary follow-up linked to each case.
gaps.impact: Seizure is an intervention measure; it cannot be converted into animals saved or suffering avoided.

gaps.detail: §48 video offenses predate PACT. Herrera's 2023 video case illustrates implementation of the current statute but does not isolate what the 2019 conduct offense newly enabled.
gaps.neededData: Charging instruments, judgments, offense subsections and legal counterfactual analysis.
gaps.impact: Do not credit every post-2019 cruelty or video prosecution to the PACT expansion.

gaps.detail: Legacy uscode.house.gov view.xhtml endpoints returned page-not-found/maintenance; CDN requests sometimes timed out. New /us/usc/119-121/ routes resolved current Code. Original Supreme Court slip-opinion link failed; official GovInfo U.S. Reports version was used.
gaps.neededData: Archive retrieved documents and hashes; refresh working endpoints. Obtain sentencing judgments for agency-only case records.
gaps.impact: Current source links are recorded; primary legal opinions are available, but case releases remain agency claims rather than independent case audits.

gaps.detail: Inspections target selected shows and entries; repeat horses and overlapping DQP/APHIS groups are not resolved. A rise in detections can reflect targeting or protocol changes.
gaps.neededData: Event-, entry- and horse-level linked data, selection probabilities, consistent diagnostics and a comparison group.
gaps.impact: HPA rates describe recorded detection, not national soring prevalence or causal presidential performance.

gaps.detail: The 2024 rule includes VMO referrals to DQPs; event-activity reports use narrower reporting. The two-veterinarian confirmation requirement ended in 2021.
gaps.neededData: A reconciliation crosswalk across annual event reports, referrals, case dispositions and diagnostic protocols.
gaps.impact: Do not splice incompatible reports or attribute the 2021 rise wholly to changing horse welfare.

gaps.topic: AWA data quality and changing operations
gaps.detail: OIG documented unreliable ACIS queries, manual reports and complaint-follow-up weaknesses. eFile replaced ACIS in 2020; pandemic and virtual inspections changed surveillance.
gaps.neededData: Validated entity identifiers, unique-facility coverage, standardized inspection types and animal-exposure denominators.
gaps.impact: Inspection and enforcement trends are implementation evidence with structural breaks.

gaps.detail: Budget prefaces explicitly specify fiscal years unless otherwise noted. CRS separately reports 254 cases/205 warnings for 2022 versus budget FY2022 counts of 262/204; the source discrepancy is unresolved.
gaps.neededData: A versioned APHIS reconciliation of CRS, budget, impact-report and IES figures.
gaps.impact: Use the verified fiscal budget series consistently; do not substitute unreconciled CRS figures.

gaps.detail: Official quarterly-workbook catalog was identified, but direct FSIS page retrieval returned access failure and no workbooks were extracted.
gaps.neededData: Downloadable quarterly humane-handling tasks, NRs, HATS hours and egregious-event data with matching definitions.
gaps.impact: No claim of complete annual FY2021–FY2025 FSIS enforcement trends; historical GAO and 2018–2020 letters are the verified evidence.

gaps.detail: No retrieved causal national evaluation isolates the 2013 pet-sales, 2020 dog-care, downer-cattle, veal or organic standards from inspection intensity, private audits, market change and other laws.
gaps.neededData: Animal-level health/behavior/injury outcomes, exposure populations, adoption dates and credible comparison groups.
gaps.impact: Legal scope and implementation cannot be translated into numbers of animals helped or net presidential scores.

gaps.detail: Latest annual APHIS enforcement output is FY2025. Comparable HPA sore-finding series ends FY2023; newer event reports through FY2025 use different columns and the FY2025 snapshot predates fiscal year-end. Organic/HPA transitions extend beyond cutoff.
gaps.neededData: Final FY2026 reports, subsequent HPA effective-date records and post-compliance organic audits.
gaps.impact: Do not imply complete 2026 coverage or realized benefits from future effective dates.

gaps.detail: Six selected trial plants reported task-level humane-handling data with no contemporaneous comparison group. The latest verified implementation update is August 5, 2026; an October search identified no later final rule.
gaps.neededData: Plant-level exposure, line speeds, observed handling outcomes, comparable controls and latest docket disposition.
gaps.impact: 11/25,821 is an agency verification-task ratio, not a pig-abuse rate or proof of safety; proposed changes remain distinct from implemented rules.

gaps.detail: The public-search restoration is verified but completeness and historical redaction are not independently audited here.
gaps.neededData: Archived portal snapshots, completeness audit and research linking access to corrective action.
gaps.impact: Transparency is a plausible mechanism, not a measured welfare gain.

gaps.detail: The five-year ARS series reports registered facilities and annual inspection visits; the facility portfolio changes and does not represent all research establishments.
gaps.neededData: Facility-level panel and standardized incident severities.
gaps.impact: Visits per facility are workload; detected noncompliance fractions are neither animal-harm rates nor generalizable nationally.

gaps.detail: No complete comparable annual count of all U.S. laboratory animals was verified in this review; APHIS excludes several major populations and NIH's October 2026 expansion remains a proposal.
gaps.neededData: Annual institution/species counts with stable definitions, duplicates removed and noncovered animals included.

gaps.topic: Conflicting NOAA records for 2019 shark-fin imports
gaps.detail: 2020 Atlantic HMS SAFE, published March 2021, Table 8.30, printed p. 211 (PDF p. 234), records preliminary 2019 imports of 1 metric ton total: dried 0, fresh 1, frozen 0 (rw-s-shark-safe2020). The 2024 Shark Finning Report p. 8 states no imports since 2019 (rw-s-shark-report), which may mean after 2019 or reflect revisions. The reason is unverified. The 2019 observation is marked missing/disputed with value null; no source value is silently selected.
gaps.neededData: Reconcile customs product codes, raw trade records, revision history and NOAA explanation of the 2019 boundary year.
gaps.impact: Exclude 2019 from numeric charts and before/after calculations pending reconciliation; retain the documented conflict. The explicit 2023 zero-export observation remains supported.
